([[Ypsilanti, Michigan]]) * Ypsi Prep Academy
(Ypsilanti, Michigan) | college = * [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (2021–2022) * [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] (2022–present) | highlights = * Third-team All-[[Mid-American Conference|MAC]] (2023) * [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] (2020) }} '''Emoni James-Wayne Bates''' (born January 28, 2004) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan Eagles]] of the [[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC). He previously played for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. In his first two years of high school, Bates played basketball for [[Lincoln High School (Ypsilanti, Michigan)|Lincoln High School]] in his hometown of [[Ypsilanti, Michigan]], where he was heavily touted by the national media and rated as the top [[college recruiting|recruit]] in his class. He led Lincoln to a state championship as a freshman and became the first sophomore to win the [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] boys' award. For his junior season, Bates transferred to Ypsi Prep Academy, a new school created by his father. A former [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] commit, he opted to graduate early from high school and start his college career at [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]]. As a freshman at Memphis, Bates missed time with injuries and fell sharply in [[NBA draft]] projections after not meeting expectations. He transferred to his hometown team [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] for his sophomore season. ==Early life and career== Bates was born in the [[University of Michigan]] hospital in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan|Ann Arbor]].{{cite web |last=Lage |first=Larry |title=The Next One? 13-Year-Old Hoops Phenom Takes Us On A Journey |url=https://detroit.cbslocal.com/2017/09/21/the-next-one-13-year-old-hoops-phenom-takes-us-on-a-journey/ |website=[[WWJ-TV]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=September 21, 2017}} He began playing basketball from age three,{{cite web |last=Goricki |first=David |title=Michigan's Bates is hoops prodigy, nation's No. 1 7th-grader |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2017/01/26/michigans-bates-hoops-prodigy-nations-no-1-7th-grader/97116086/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=January 27, 2017}} often sleeping with a miniature basketball under his arm and [[dribbling#basketball|dribbling]] around his house.{{cite web |last=Niyo |first=John |title=Can 'relentless' freshman Emoni Bates jump straight to NBA? |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/columnists/john-niyo/2018/12/25/ypsilanti-lincoln-hoops-star-bates-best-9th-grader-country/2374130002/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=December 26, 2018}} In his childhood, Bates trained for basketball with his father, a former professional player, by shooting around and improving his agility through various drills. In fourth grade, he played against high school seniors at a [[rec league]] in [[Saline, Michigan]] and started competing on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit.{{cite web |last=McCabe |first=Mick |title=Here's how Emoni Bates became best freshman basketball player in U.S. |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/02/14/emoni-bates-top-high-school-freshman-basketball-nba-draft/2860351002/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=February 15, 2019}} Bates also played [[association football|soccer]] while in elementary school. Bates first surfaced on the national radar in early 2016, after averaging 28 points and 12 rebounds per game for the Toledo Wildcats AAU team at a tournament in [[Chicago]].{{cite web |title=Meet the Ypsilanti basketball phenom who has America on notice |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/meet-the-ypsilanti-basketball-phenom-who-has-america-on-notice |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=February 8, 2017}} He grew from {{convert|6|ft|2|in|m|2}} to {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|2}} from sixth to seventh grade. Bates played basketball for Clague Middle School in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where as a seventh-grader, he was rated the number one player in the 2022 class by recruiting website Future150. He averaged 46 points per game in seventh grade and sat out his eighth grade season to train individually. In the summer of 2018, Bates averaged 17 points per game facing older competition at the under-15 division of the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL), a notable summer circuit.{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=USA Basketball: 2022 wing Emoni Bates navigates through early hype |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/usa-basketball-2022-wing-emoni-bates-navigates-through-early-hype |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=October 6, 2018}} ==High school career== ===Freshman season=== [[File:Emoni Bates (cropped) 2.jpg|thumb|205px|left|Bates with Bates Fundamentals at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Nike EYBL]] in May 2019]] Bates enrolled at [[Lincoln High School (Ypsilanti, Michigan)|Lincoln High School]] in [[Ypsilanti, Michigan]], being drawn there because the head basketball coach, Jesse Davis, was a longtime teammate and friend of Bates' father.{{cite web |last=Farrell |first=Perry A. |title=Why top basketball prospect Emoni Bates will attend Ypsilanti Lincoln |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/07/07/emoni-bates-ypsilanti-lincoln/756079002/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=July 8, 2018}} On November 26, 2018, Bates made his freshman season debut, recording 32 points and 15 rebounds in an 80–69 win over [[Huron High School (Ann Arbor, Michigan)|Ann Arbor Huron]] at the Ypsilanti Tip-Off Classic.{{cite web |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |title=Ypsilanti Lincoln's Emoni Bates, nation's top-ranked freshman, scores 32 in debut |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/ann-arbor/2018/11/ypsilanti_lincoln_emoni_bates.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=November 27, 2018}} On January 18, 2019, he scored a then career-high 43 points, shooting 13-of-27 from the field, in a 68–56 victory over [[Ypsilanti Community High School]].{{cite web |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |title=Lincoln's star freshman Emoni Bates scores career-high 43 in win over Ypsilanti |url=https://expo.mlive.com/sports/g66l-2019/01/f94b9c83096840/lincolns-star-freshman-emoni-bates-scores-careerhigh-43-in-win-over-ypsilanti.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=January 19, 2019}} Bates, on February 5, was ejected and suspended one game for his role in an altercation during a game versus [[Dexter High School (Michigan)|Dexter High School]].{{cite web |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |title=Ypsilanti Lincoln standout Emoni Bates set for return after suspension |url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/ann-arbor/2019/02/ypsilanti-lincoln-standout-emoni-bates-set-for-return-after-suspension.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=February 11, 2019}} On February 18, he posted 36 points and 19 rebounds in a 73–65 win over [[Jackson High School (Michigan)|Jackson High School]] to capture the [[Michigan High School Athletic Association]] (MHSAA) [[Southeastern Conference (MHSAA)|Southeastern Conference]] White division title.{{cite web |last=Goricki |first=David |title=Freshman phenom Emoni Bates helps Ypsilanti Lincoln clinch SEC White championship |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/2019/02/19/freshman-phenom-emoni-bates-helps-ypsilanti-lincoln-clinch-sec-white-championship/2920707002/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=February 19, 2019}} On March 7, he led all scorers with 36 points and made the game-winning shot in an 81–79 victory over [[Detroit Catholic Central High School]], as Lincoln claimed its first regional championship.{{cite web |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |title='Superman' Emoni Bates hits another game-winner for Lincoln's 1st regional title |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2019/03/superman-emoni-bates-hits-another-game-winner-for-lincolns-1st-regional-title.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=March 7, 2019}} Nine days later, Bates guided Lincoln to its first MHSAA Division 1 state title after scoring 23 points in a 64–62 win over top-seeded [[University of Detroit Jesuit High School and Academy]].{{cite web |last=McCabe |first=Mick |last2=Sulonen |first2=Dana |title=Emoni Bates after state title victory: 'I've got three more to win' |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/emoni-bates-after-championship-ive-got-three-more-to-win |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=March 16, 2019}} He finished the season averaging 28.5 points and 10.2 rebounds per game, helping his team to a 23–4 record.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=2018–19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Freshman All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/OprYR7BMzk6w7vB7GJ-FmA/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-freshman-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=April 19, 2019}} Bates was named Michigan [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and [[MaxPreps National Basketball Freshman of the Year|MaxPreps National Freshman of the Year]].{{cite web |last=Paul |first=Tony |title=Ypsilanti Lincoln freshman Emoni Bates named Michigan's Gatorade player of the year |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/19/ypsilanti-lincoln-freshman-emoni-bates-named-michigan-gatorade-player-year/3216408002/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 |date=March 19, 2019}} He also earned [[Associated Press]] (AP) Division 1 Player of the Year and All-State first team honors.{{cite web |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |title=Meet the Associated Press Division 1 boys basketball all-state team |url=https://expo.mlive.com/sports/g66l-2019/03/0e39ab0de85990/meet-the-associated-press-division-1-boys-basketball-allstate-team.html |first=Mick |title=Emoni Bates proves why he's the best freshman to ever play in Michigan |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/high-school/mick-mccabe/2019/03/15/emoni-bates-mhsaa-michigan-high-school-basketball/3154582002/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=July 14, 2019 Meet the 15-Year-Old Next in Line |url=https://www.si.com/high-school/2019/10/29/emoni-bates-nba-draft-prospect-kevin-durant |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 24, 2020 |date=October 29, 2019}} In his season debut, he scored 24 points but was held to 6-of-21 shooting in a loss to River Rouge High School.{{cite web |last=Goricki |first=David |title=Monday's preps: River Rouge upstages Ypsilanti Lincoln, Emoni Bates |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/09/mondays-preps-river-rouge-upstages-ypsilanti-lincoln-bates-63-53/4381697002/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=December 10, 2019 |date=December 10, 2019}} On January 17, 2020, Bates scored 40 points in a 67–38 victory over Dexter High School.{{cite web |last=Wickliffe |first=Greg |title=Watch Emoni Bates explode for 40 points in win over Dexter |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2020/01/watch-emoni-bates-explode-for-40-points-in-win-over-dexter.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=January 25, 2020 |date=January 17, 2020}} He tallied 42 points on January 27 in an 83–56 win over Jackson High School. |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2020/03/emoni-bates-father-agrees-with-mhsaas-decision-kids-safety-comes-first.html |publisher=MLive |access-date=April 14, 2020 |date=March 12, 2020}} As a record.{{cite web |last=Wickliffe |first=Greg |title=Emoni Bates named finalist for Gatorade National Boys Basketball Player of the Year 2020}} Bates was recognized as [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]], becoming the first sophomore to win the boys' version of the award,{{efn|The first player to |date=April 9, 2020}} ===Junior season=== Before his junior season, Bates announced that he would transfer to Ypsi Prep Academy, a new prep school in Ypsilanti created by his father.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |last2=Schlabach |first2=Mark |title=Emoni Bates, 2022 top recruit, commits to Michigan State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29383554 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 29, 2020 |date=June 29, 2020}} On November 12, 2020, he made his debut with the program, scoring 36 points in a 78–71 [[exhibition game]] loss to [[Chet Holmgren]] and Team Sizzle.{{cite web |last=Schoch |first=Matt |title=Emoni Bates scores 36 in Ypsi Prep Academy debut; Michigan target Chet Holmgren dominates |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/11/12/msu-recruit-emoni-bates-scores-36-espn-2-ypsi-prep-loses-78-71/3761097001/ |website=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=May 1, 2021 |date=November 12, 2020}} As a junior, Bates averaged 23 points, 5.8 rebounds, three assists and 2.2 steals per game, leading his team to a 7–3 record. He was one of five finalists for the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award]].{{cite web |last=Wickliffe |first=Greg |title=Emoni Bates among 5 finalists for Naismith HS Player of the Year award |url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/2021/02/emoni-bates-among-5-finalists-for-naismith-hs-player-of-the-year-award.html |website=MLive |access-date=May 1, 2021 |date=February 20, 2021}} After the season, he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] up to the 2021 class and bypassed his senior year of high school.{{cite web |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |title=How Emoni Bates survived the early hype and remained a top NBA prospect |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2021/8/25/22639585/emoni-bates-scouting-report-recruiting-nba-draft-coaching |website=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=August 25, 2021 |date=August 25, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Bates was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web |title=Emoni Bates |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/238280 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 27, 2023 |date=July 19, 2019}} He received a scholarship offer from [[NCAA Division I]] program [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] in eighth grade. After his freshman season in high school, Bates was offered scholarships by [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] and [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]].{{cite web |last=Solari |first=Chris |title=Michigan State basketball offers scholarship to phenom Emoni Bates |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2019/07/12/michigan-state-basketball-emoni-bates-scholarship-offer/1716427001/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=August 7, 2019 |date=July 12, 2019}}{{cite web |last=Sang |first=Orion |title=Michigan basketball offers scholarship to phenom Emoni Bates |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2019/07/18/michigan-basketball-recruiting-emoni-bates-offer/1767328001/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=August 7, 2019 |date=July 18, 2019}}{{cite web |last=Giles |first=Matt |title='Six-star' Emoni Bates lands Duke basketball offer, likes Blue Devils |url=https://balldurham.com/2019/08/22/emoni-bates-duke-basketball-offer-likes/ |website=Ball Durham |access-date=January 24, 2020 |date=August 22, 2019}} By then, he was being touted by analysts and scouts as the top high school basketball prospect regardless of class.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Why 15-year-old Emoni Bates is basketball's next phenomenon |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/insider/story/_/id/27332999 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=August 7, 2019 |date=August 7, 2019}} Following Bates' junior season, however, [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] remarked that he "looks to have hit a bit of a roadblock in his development." |last=Goldberg |first=Rob |title=5-Star SF Emoni Bates Commits to Michigan State; Ranked No. 1 in Class of 2022 2020}} He was drawn to the program by head coach [[Tom Izzo]] and the school's coaching staff, who had been building a relationship with him since he was in seventh grade. At the time, Bates was the highest rated recruit to commit to Michigan State in the modern recruiting era.
